name: Amortized Analysis
description: Amortized analysis averages the cost of a sequence of operations over the entire sequence, showing that even if some individual operations are expensive, the average cost per operation is low. It explains why a dynamic array append is 'O(1) amortized' despite occasional O(N) re-sizes.
key_points: Amortized ≠ average-case over inputs; it is a worst-case bound over a sequence.
Dynamic arrays double their capacity; N appends cost O(N) total → O(1) each.
Hash tables rehash at a load factor; insertions are O(1) amortized.
std::vector / Python list growth is the canonical example.
examples: Append to a resizable array — O(1) amortized
Incrementing a binary counter — O(1) amortized
Union-Find with path compression + union by rank — near O(1) amortized
common_mistakes: Saying an operation is always O(1) when it is only amortized O(1).
Confusing amortized analysis with average-case analysis.
